objective: Equity book v1.3 candidate: can a preregistered cost-aware trading rule (Garleanu-Pedersen partial adjustment at rate 1/2 or 1/3, the same on the unit book with the VIX scale applied at once, or a Novy-Marx-Velikov style no-trade band of 0.25 / 0.50 weight SD) raise the net Sharpe of the unchanged v1.2 primary book M0_U3000 by at least 0.10 in both the recent (2024-01-08..2026-09-15) and the stress (2017-10-02..2023-08-31) window, against full rebalancing (B0, R6 identity), with a paired Newey-West t >= 2, and keep the gain in the account layer (whole shares, $100 minimum order) so the paper book trades cheaper without changing its signal.

sources.core_claim: Garleanu and Pedersen (NBER w15205, 2009; Journal of Finance 2013): with predictable returns and transaction costs the optimal policy trades partially towards an aim portfolio at a fixed rate a/lambda < 1 that falls with costs and rises with risk aversion (Proposition 2, eq. 7-10); the aim is an exponential average of current and expected future Markowitz portfolios, so predictors with slower alpha decay get more weight (Proposition 3). In their commodity-futures application (Table II, benchmark costs) the Markowitz portfolio has gross Sharpe 0.83 and net -9.84, the dynamic optimum 0.62 gross / 0.58 net, and the best static partial-adjustment rule (3% weight on Markowitz per day) 0.58 / 0.46; the dynamic net Sharpe is about 20% above the best static strategy because it under-weights the fast (2.4-day half-life) signal.
sources.project_applicability: Rules P2, P3 and P2V are the static fixed-rate form of Proposition 2 applied per tranche to the unchanged M0 target; the persistence-tilted aim (Proposition 3) is deferred to a later contract because it changes the composite.
sources.reflection: Commodity futures, daily data, quadratic costs and a 5-day signal; our book is weekly, mostly slow signals, with spread plus square-root impact, so the size of the gain does not transfer, only the form of the rule.

sources.core_claim: Novy-Marx and Velikov (A Taxonomy of Anomalies and Their Trading Costs, August 2015 version; RFS 2016), 1973-2012 with effective-spread costs: a buy/hold spread (a stricter rule to enter a position than to keep it, e.g. 10%/20% deciles) is the most effective cost-mitigation technique; for a UMD-like factor it earns 0.77%/month gross, 0.26% costs, 0.51% net, against 0.62 / 0.26 / 0.37 for staggered quarterly partial rebalancing and 0.66 / 0.35 / 0.31 for trading only a low-cost universe (Table 5): the same cost saving as lower-frequency staggered rebalancing while giving up less gross return.
sources.project_applicability: Rules N25 and N50 are the continuous-weight analogue (a no-trade band around each name's target); v1.2's five weekly tranches are already a form of staggered partial rebalancing, which this paper ranks below the buy/hold spread.
sources.reflection: Decile sorts with monthly rebalancing and 1973-2012 effective spreads; a band on continuous rank weights is an analogue, not the tested rule; 10%/20% in rank terms is roughly a 0.44 standard-deviation band in normal scores at the 80th-90th percentile, which motivates the 0.25 and 0.50 band sizes.

sources.core_claim: Jensen, Kelly, Malamud and Pedersen (SFI 22-63, 2022 version; RFS 2026): portfolios that put ML return forecasts, risk and trading costs into one objective keep positive out-of-sample net Sharpe ratios, reaching 1.38 for Portfolio-ML for an investor whose wealth reaches $10 billion by 2020, while cost-agnostic Markowitz portfolios fall to negative net returns.
sources.project_applicability: Sets the realistic ceiling for a cost-aware book and supports one optimizer holding alpha, risk and costs (design section 8); M3 (random-feature ridge) follows this line. v1.3: eq. (20) starts from the grown (drifted) position and trades toward an aim, the form of rules P2/P3/P2V.
sources.reflection: 2022 working-paper version (the RFS 2026 numbers may differ); price-impact costs only; a $10 billion large-cap investor, not a $1M U3000 book; the full model set needs about 75 GB, so we run a reduced version.

sources.core_claim: AQR Alternative Thinking 2023 Issue 4, Exhibit A1 (Hedge Fund Research data, May 1996 - August 2023, net of fees, 87 systematic and 337 discretionary long/short equity funds including dead funds): systematic funds' Sharpe ratio is 0 / 0.2 / 0.51 / 0.87 / 1.18 at the 10th / 25th / median / 75th / 90th percentile, with median beta 0.08.
sources.project_applicability: Calibrates the target: a book net Sharpe of 0.5-1.0 is the professional median to 75th percentile, and K1's 1.19 anchor bar sits at the systematic 90th percentile.
sources.reflection: Manager-written note; fund returns are net of fees while our book has no fees but no institutional execution either; global funds, not US-only; exact publication date not printed in the snapshot.

sources.core_claim: Chen and Velikov (JFQA 58(3), May 2023): after effective bid-ask spreads, post-publication decay and restricting to the post-2005 trading-technology era, the average published anomaly is expected to earn just 4 bp per month net; the strongest anomalies net at best about 10 bp, and several methods for combining anomalies net around 20 bp.
sources.project_applicability: Single anomalies are not worth trading alone after costs; only cost-aware combinations can clear the bar, which is why the book replaces standalone anomaly tests.
sources.reflection: Spread costs only (no impact, no short-sale fees); anomaly portfolios as published; the date is the issue month.

sources.core_claim: Frazzini, Israel and Moskowitz ('Trading Costs', SSRN 3229719, August 2018 draft): on 1.7 trillion dollars of live executions by a large institutional manager across 21 developed equity markets over 19 years, price impact is well approximated by a square-root function of trade size, and actual trading costs are an order of magnitude smaller than previous studies suggest.
sources.project_applicability: Supports the impact term Y * sigma_daily * sqrt(Q/V) with Y = 0.5 in cost model v1 (design section 7) and the small impact at a $1M book.
sources.reflection: Proprietary execution data, not replicable; algorithmic institutional execution, not market-on-open orders at the first print; month-level date.

sources.core_claim: Jensen, Kelly and Pedersen (JF 2023): on a new global data set of 153 factors across 93 countries, most asset pricing factors can be replicated, cluster into 13 themes and work out of sample.
sources.project_applicability: Supports theme-level composites (M0 equal-weights themes) and the theme list of signal library v1.
sources.reflection: Gross factor returns; replication is not net profitability (see Chen-Velikov); the snapshot does not print the issue date.

sources.core_claim: Alpaca margin and short-selling documentation (fetched 2026-10-02): a Reg T margin account may hold up to 2x equity in marginable securities overnight and receives a margin call the next morning if initial (50%) and maintenance requirements are not met at the end of the day; maintenance is 30% for longs above $6 and the greater of $5.00/share or 30% for shorts at $5 or more; easy-to-borrow shares carry $0 locate and borrow fees for Trading API users while hard-to-borrow shorts need an approved locate; margin interest is 5.00% (elite) or 6.50% (non-elite) on the end-of-day debit balance.
sources.project_applicability: Fixes the account layer of v1.2: total gross including the SPY hedge and the T-bill leg capped at 1.8x equity (Reg T 2x minus a 10% buffer), the Alpaca maintenance table for the end-of-day margin check, borrow 0 bp on easy-to-borrow shorts, debit interest 6.50% a year for F2.
sources.reflection: HTML page without a version date (published_or_updated_at unknown); rates and the ETB fee policy can change; paper accounts may not enforce every rule, so the simulation enforces them itself.

hypothesis.statement: The v1.2 primary book loses about 0.24 Sharpe (recent) and 0.18 (stress) to costs and borrow; its main themes are slow (value, quality, investment, momentum, low risk), so trading partially towards the target or inside a no-trade band should cut cost by more than it delays alpha.
hypothesis.failure_mode: Alpha decays within one or two weeks (seasonality and short-volume themes, rank noise that is real signal), or the VIX halving loses its protection when smoothed, so the net gain is below +0.10 in at least one window; or the account layer's $100 minimum order and whole shares already remove the small trades the rules save.
hypothesis.measurement: Offset-median and blended net Sharpe per rule and window, Δ vs B0 per offset, paired NW t of the blended daily net difference, turnover, cost, gross exposure, realized beta, 2x cost; Stage 2 account-layer F1 overlay Sharpe and F2 IR, other variants, family DSR tier, 20-seed placebo.
hypothesis.stop_pivot: No rule meets E1 (+0.10 both windows): keep v1.2 full rebalancing, record the frontier and the death cause; a persistence-tilted aim (GP Proposition 3, a composite change) is the only follow-up and needs a new contract.

decision.reason: Preregistered 2026-10-04 by the 01:07 UTC lead round before any rule was run; executed by brief T-20261004-01.
decision.next_iteration_suggestion: If a rule replaces B0: production target generator change in a separate task, switch after the v1.2 two-week execution shakedown at a monthly rescoring. If none: GP aim tilt by theme persistence, preregistered from the return-free diagnostics of this task.
